Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2977); Josias (i.e. Joshiah), an Israelite:--Josias.
BiblicalUsage: Josias is the Greek form of Josiah, the boy king who found the book of the law. In Matthew 1:10 Ezekias begat Manasses, and Manasses begat Amon, and Amon begat Josias, and in Matthew 1:11 Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Josias is the brightest king in the list: eight years old when he took the throne, and the man who tore down the idols and read the book to the people.
